name: Benchmark Predictive Model (BPM) for Arctic sea ice forecasting
description: We propose a reduced-form benchmark predictive model (BPM) for fixed-target forecasting of Arctic sea ice extent, and we provide a case study of its real-time performance for target date September 2020. We visually detail the evolution of the statistically-optimal point, interval, and density forecasts as time passes, new information arrives, and the end of September approaches. Comparison to the BPM may prove useful for evaluating and selecting among various more sophisticated dynamical sea ice models, which are widely used to quantify the likely future evolution of Arctic conditions and their two-way interaction with economic activity.
general_score_metric: RMSE (with CRPS reported for probabilistic forecasts)
reputation: A research-oriented baseline proposed in the climate science literature as a reduced-form benchmark for Arctic sea-ice forecasting; it is a useful reference but not a broadly adopted community standard.
notes: Non-LLM, small-scale/reduced-form benchmark used as a baseline; case-study focused on a single target date (Sept 2020) so sample size is limited. Designed as a simple statistical comparator for more complex dynamical models; potential overfitting/selection risk if widely used without cross-validation.
